definition: Beseech means to beg or plead desperately, with pride set aside and everything at stake.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word beseech. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know beseech should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The letter from the front does not ask so much as beseech: send word, send anything, tell me you are alive.
Urge sits well below beseech — to urge is to press with composure and move on, the way a doctor urges rest and heads to the next chart, while to beseech is to plead with the pride stripped out.
Grovel goes further than beseech — the pleading collapses into self-abasement, forehead to the floor, dignity traded away entirely.

To implore is to plead with desperate urgency — a near twin of beseech, only a shade more bookish. Both belong to moments when everything is at stake and pride has stopped mattering; if the asking is calm or routine, neither word fits.

To entreat is to ask earnestly and gently, almost humbly — the asker looks up at the person being asked, and an entreaty can still be declined politely. To beseech is that plea grown desperate, all pride set aside, the voice already breaking.

To petition is to ask an authority through proper form — a written request, signatures, the official channel. To beseech is raw and personal: one voice pleading with the pride stripped out. A petition can sit in an in-box for weeks; beseeching happens in the moment, out loud.
